title: Sweet Chilli Crispy Cauliflower
subtitle: with Colourful Capsicums and Microwave Rice
description: Whether you're full-time vego or part-time only, our varied range of vegetarian dishes really hits the spot. Bursting with veggies, dairy, legumes, grains and nuts, they're packed with flavour, they’ll fill you up and they're totally mouth-watering too!

steps.text: Prep ingredients: Thinly slice the spring onion. Cut the capsicums into 1cm chunks. Coarsely chop the cauliflower stem, then cut the head into small florets. Put the cornflour in a large bowl and gradually whisk in 2 tbs water until you have a smooth and loose batter (see Cooking tip).

Fry cauliflower: Heat 2cm vegetable oil in a medium deep frypan over medium-high heat. Using tongs, dip the cauliflower into the batter, then shake off the excess. Carefully add the cauliflower to the hot oil and cook for 5-6 mins until golden and cooked through. Remove from the pan and drain on a wire rack set over paper towel. Discard the oil and wipe the pan clean.

Cook capsicum: Combine the sweet chilli sauce, 1 tbs tomato sauce and 2 tsp soy sauce in a bowl and season with pepper. Heat 1 tsp vegetable oil in the same pan over medium-high heat. Cook the capsicum, stirring occasionally, for 5 mins or until softened. Add the sauce mixture and cauliflower and cook for 1 min or until the sauce coats the vegetables.
Fry eggs: Meanwhile, heat 1 tsp vegetable oil in a medium frypan over medium heat. Crack 2 eggs into the pan and cook for 3-4 mins until just set or cooked to your liking.

Heat rice and serve up: Massage the packet of rice to loosen and tear a 2cm opening for the steam to escape. Heat in the microwave for 90 secs or until warmed through. Divide the rice and cauliflower and capsicum mixture among bowls. Top with the fried eggs and scatter with the spring onion. Enjoy!

Did you know?: This dish is inspired by an Indo-Chinese dish called Gobi Manchurian. It's made by deep-frying lightly battered cauliflower (and other vegetables), then coating them in a soy- flavoured sauce.
